HOW_TO_VERIFY_THIS_SEAL.verified_at_seal: PASS — recomputed and matched before this field was written; the script asserts, so this entry could not exist otherwise
HOW_TO_VERIFY_THIS_SEAL.prefix_bound_from_the_start: flight records get appended to preregs after sealing, so a whole-file sha256 would MISMATCH a seal that was perfectly honoured. Bound to the first N bytes and stated as an executable command.

AUTHOR_CLAIMS_VERIFIED_NOT_ACCEPTED.how: re-derived from the sealed bytes: gate labels by regex over the frozen text, three-state and fault-coverage language by presence, and the no-truncatable-literal claim by searching for ANY constant written to 4+ decimals — there are none. Every decimal in the prereg (0.10, 0.5, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 1.0) is a GATE BAR compared against a measured dial, not a golden value compared against a tolerance.

THE_DESIGN_FORECLOSES_THIS_CAMPAIGNS_OWN.truncated_fence_constant: the §3 ideals are the INTEGERS 0 and 1, so the registered 1e-9 KA tolerance is satisfiable BY CONSTRUCTION — an integer has no truncation error. This is the defect that cost B1's first flight 11 QPU-seconds, designed out rather than guarded against.
THE_DESIGN_FORECLOSES_THIS_CAMPAIGNS_OWN.depth_blowup: the pair decoder is GF(4)-LINEAR, so every dial pub is Z-basis + classical XOR and no Helstrom rotation exists anywhere in the flight, max pub ~35 CX. B1's depth HOLD fired at 190 on a generic 4-qubit joint rotation; here the instrument is chosen so the hold cannot fire.
THE_DESIGN_FORECLOSES_THIS_CAMPAIGNS_OWN.stale_gate_input: co-batched into a SINGLE job, so gate-geometry edge 4 (validity) degenerates to zero window — staleness impossible by construction, not unlikely by policy.
THE_DESIGN_FORECLOSES_THIS_CAMPAIGNS_OWN.unpowerable_or_trivially_passable_gates: five THREE-STATE gates with a registered FAULT-COVERAGE MATRIX: each computed fault names the gate that catches it. Mask-stuck breaks blindness and fails G1's singles cap at 1.0 vs 0.10; the dial-INVISIBLE no-b encoding fault leaves every dial ideal and kills G3 revival to exactly 0; a dead apparatus fails the G2 positive control; scramble-leak fails G4.

SEAL_TIME_CHECKS_RUN.[7] dual-representation edges in spec: CLEAR — no edge stated both as a value and an approximation
SEAL_TIME_CHECKS_RUN.[3] registered bars in flight code: SKIPPED, and the skip is the finding
SEAL_TIME_CHECKS_RUN.WHY_3_WAS_SKIPPED_AND_WHY_IT_MATTERS: There is no A1 flight script yet — it is built after the seal. Pointed at the $0 SIMULATION scout, the checker first emitted FIVE 'registered bar NOT FOUND in flight code' hits, every one an artifact mismatch, including a '1e-9 vs 1e-14' that was a numerical-noise cutoff inside an exact sim rather than a fence tolerance. I caught it by checking WHAT THE FILE WAS before drawing a conclusion from it. Had I not, I would have posted five defects against a prereg whose author had just correctly told me its fence targets are integers by construction. A CHECKER THAT SILENTLY ACCEPTS THE WRONG ARTIFACT MANUFACTURES FINDINGS, and manufactured findings are worse than none — they spend the reader's trust and train them to discount the real ones. Guard [0] now classifies on whether the file SUBMITS and skips [3] when it does not.
